rule.description: A function or method absorbs the implementation of another function defined in the same file - either verbatim (modulo consistent renaming of local variables) or with that other function's own same-file sub-calls expanded - so the implementation now lives twice and the absorbing body carries the structural complexity of its sub-methods.

checks.description: The absorbing function's body contains a contiguous copy of a same-file source function's implementation as written, equal modulo consistent renaming of local variables.
checks.detected_relation: absorbing owner F -> same-file source function G whose raw body appears in F's body
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The implementation of G now exists twice in the file: once as G, once pasted into F. The absorbing method does the work of G itself instead of delegating.

matches.evidence: RouteLeg::from embeds the body of RouteStep::from_maneuver (the step construction: banner text, maneuvers, struct literal) inside the windows(3).map closure, while RouteStep::from_maneuver still exists and is still called for the first and last steps of the leg.

RouteLeg::from_leg embeds the body of RouteStep::from_maneuver (with v6 distance-unit threading) inside its middle-step closure, while RouteStep::from_maneuver still exists and is still used for the first and last steps.

Leg::from_otp embeds the body of build_verbal_post_transition_instruction (the if-distance-is-zero/Continue-for format) at the step loop, while build_verbal_post_transition_instruction remains in the file.

Leg::from_otp embeds the body of leg_duration_seconds (leg.duration.unwrap_or_else with the best_estimate elapsed-time fallback) at the step loop, while leg_duration_seconds remains in the file and is still called by the transit-leg path.
verify_feed embeds the body of fetch_feed (authenticated_request, send, error_for_status, bytes) in its own download block, while fetch_feed remains in the file and is still called by measure().

RouterConfig::for_zone embeds the body of the free function credential (authorization.option unwrap, secret lookup, SkippedRealtime, AuthKindSecret::resolve) as a local closure, while the free function credential remains in the file.
RouterConfig::for_zone embeds the body of the free function otp_updater (the StreamKind -> updater name/frequency match) as an inline match, while the free function otp_updater remains in the file.

list_feeds embeds the body of summarize (filter_map id -> FeedSummary with realtime summaries, bbox, area, relevance) as a block expression feeding its sort, while summarize remains in the file and is still called by feeds_by_id.

checks.description: The absorbing function's body contains a same-file source function's implementation with that source function's OWN same-file sub-calls expanded inline, producing the depth-3 shape where a sub-method and its sub-sub-methods are all pasted into one caller.
checks.detected_relation: absorbing owner F -> same-file source G whose flat body (G's body with G's own same-file sub-calls expanded) appears in F's body
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: F carries not just G but G's sub-methods, fully expanded, so a single function embodies a three-level call chain whose extraction boundaries have been erased.

matches.evidence: RouteLeg::from contains RouteStep::from_maneuver's body with from_maneuver's own call to VisualInstructionBanner::from_maneuver expanded, plus that helper's banner-component assembly: the chain RouteLeg::from -> RouteStep::from_maneuver -> VisualInstructionBanner::from_maneuver -> component assembly lives in one monolithic per-step closure.

RouteLeg::from_leg contains RouteStep::from_maneuver's body with its call to VisualInstructionBanner::from_maneuver expanded (and the banner component assembly below it), v6 distance-unit threaded through: the same depth-3 chain, in the compatibility generation.

Leg::from_otp contains Maneuver::from_otp's body with its calls to maneuver_instruction (the instruction matcher now matches on leg.mode.as_ref() rather than its mode parameter), build_verbal_post_transition_instruction, and leg_duration_seconds all expanded: the chain Leg::from_otp -> Maneuver::from_otp -> {maneuver_instruction, build_verbal_post_transition_instruction, leg_duration_seconds} lives in one straight-line loop body.

excluded.reason: Same transit-plan step-assembly chain as the v7 plan site, in the older API generation. A parallel absorption would only repeat the covered role in the same shape, so it was left out for saturation rather than reach.

The upstream caller in the same plan-assembly chain; absorbing the leg loop there would repeat the covered chain one level up and inflate an already large builder without introducing a new function role.

excluded.location: cross-file duplication of gtfout::transit_zone::Zone::new, AuthKindSecret::resolve, and other library functions
excluded.reason: The rule only flags same-file duplications: cross-file/cross-crate consumption is a different relation in this codebase and is out of scope for this case.

excluded.location: macro-synthesized or closure-synthesized functions and all test modules
excluded.reason: The rule deliberately excludes generated code and cfg(test) bodies; their 'implementations' are not authored and their duplication is not this smell.

excluded.location: single-level same-file thin wrappers (e.g. elevation.rs / directions.rs request plumbing, gtfout data-model accessors)
excluded.reason: Their helpers are one call deep; absorbing them produces flat one-level duplication, not the deeply inlined shape the rule characterizes, and they were not changed.
